summary: Design, manage, and evaluate population-level mental health programmes using WHO mhGAP, Theory of Change, and DHIS2. Enrol in this 5-day public health course.
lede: Mental health programme management training helps public health managers assess service gaps and plan population-level services. It is intended for programme managers, service planners and monitoring and evaluation specialists with a public health or health-systems background, rather than clinicians. Participants practise building a theory of change and results framework, mapping stepped-care pathways to workforce capacity, and using evaluation and digital data tools to monitor programme performance.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for mid-career professionals who hold operational or advisory responsibility for mental health programmes within public health systems, health ministries, NGOs, or international health organizations. You should have a working background in public health, health system management, or a related field — this is not a clinical training course.
modules: Mental Health Burden and Public Health System Context
Programme Design: Theory of Change and Logic Models
Service Delivery Planning and Stepped-Care Models
Digital Health Tools and Real-Time Programme Monitoring
Stakeholder Engagement, Advocacy, and Resource Mobilization
Programme Integration, Reporting, and Strategic Planning
prerequisites: This course is designed for professionals with at least two years of experience in public health programme management, health system strengthening, or a related field. You should have a working familiarity with basic public health concepts (disease burden, health system levels, primary care) and general programme management principles (planning cycles, logical frameworks, reporting). No clinical mental health training or psychology background is required. No coding or data science skills are needed; digital tool sessions use guided templates and pre-configured dashboards. Participants are encouraged to bring a current or planned programme context to apply course exercises — this significantly increases the practical value of the workshop sessions.
